subject.title: fix: bind GitHub OAuth login to initiating device

question: Should this PR land the fail-closed GitHub OAuth protocol change that rejects old CLI poll-only logins, or should maintainers require a staged compatibility path before merge?
rationale: The code path is a credential-issuance security boundary and the safer fail-closed behavior deliberately changes the CLI/coordinator compatibility contract for existing clients.

options.title: Accept fail-closed security fix
options.body: Land after removing the release-owned changelog entries and explicitly accepting that old CLIs must upgrade before GitHub login works.

options.title: Require staged rollout
options.body: Ask for a maintainer-approved compatibility or rollout mechanism if old CLI login must keep working temporarily without reopening token theft.

options.title: Pause for protocol redesign
options.body: Hold the PR if maintainers prefer a PKCE-style or otherwise different OAuth binding contract.

recommendation.title: Accept fail-closed security fix
recommendation.body: Land after removing the release-owned changelog entries and explicitly accepting that old CLIs must upgrade before GitHub login works.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest recent history on the GitHub browser login and OAuth callback-binding code paths.
